definition: Indexed grammars are a generalization of context-free grammars in that nonterminals are equipped with lists of flags, or index symbols.
details: The language produced by an indexed grammar is called an indexed language.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. In plain words: Indexed grammars are a generalization of context-free grammars in that nonterminals are equipped with lists of flags, or index symbols. Here is how it actually plays out: The language produced by an indexed grammar is called an indexed language. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. And that idea, made concrete, is Indexed grammar.
